Slashed Text Generator

A diagonal stroke per character, harder to miss than a strikethrough

A diagonal stroke on every character

U+0338 puts a diagonal through every character rather than a horizontal, and the difference is more than decorative. The stroke cuts across the letterform at an angle nothing else in the alphabet uses, so the eye cannot skim past it. Where a strikethrough at small sizes can be mistaken for part of the type, a slash registers as deliberate cancellation the moment you look at it, which is the whole reason to reach for this one.

Some fonts draw the combining solidus noticeably taller than the letter beneath it, so a slashed line can crowd the line above and look cramped in a narrow column. It carries the same doubled character count as the rest of the combining marks, too. Worth it when something has to be visibly void: a cancelled date on an event listing, a rule that no longer applies, a name on a roster who is out. It is a second character per letter, not a font effect.

Also searched as: diagonal line through text, slash through letters, crossed letters.

Where Slashed text works, and where it does not

WorksWorks anywhere plain text goes, and is the only way to strike through or underline in a field that will not take formatting. Watch outEach mark is its own character, so the length counts against a bio limit even though nothing extra is visible. A few platforms strip combining marks on save.

Slashed questions

How is this different from a strikethrough?

Angle and weight. A strikethrough lays a horizontal rule at mid height, which at small sizes can be mistaken for part of the letter. The solidus cuts diagonally, crossing the letterform in a direction nothing else in the alphabet uses, so it registers as cancellation immediately even in a crowded line.

Why does the stroke stick up above the letters?

Type designers draw the combining solidus long enough to cross a tall character, and it keeps that length on a short one. On some faces the top of the slash therefore rises well above lowercase letters and nudges the line above. Most plain-text fields give you no line spacing control to compensate.

Can I slash a whole paragraph?

You can, and it will be close to unreadable, which may well be the point. Two things to weigh: every character doubles, so a long block eats a length limit quickly, and the diagonals stack into visual noise over several lines. One slashed phrase inside plain text carries far more meaning.
